text:
maria: Heads-up, hitting a reproducible packaging/install quirk with the Python SDK and Poetry editable installs. Steps: in sampleapp run `poetry install` then `python -c 'import redwood_sdk; import redwood_sdk.asyncio'` -> ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'redwood_sdk.asyncio'. The wheel built by CI contains the subpackages.

sam: Ugh, that sounds like the PEP 660 editable backend edge-case. Poetry delegates to pip for editable wheels and if package discovery metadata is underspecified, subpackages can be omitted. Can you paste your pyproject.toml snippet?

maria: Minimal pyproject: ```toml
[tool.poetry]
name = "redwood-sdk"
version = "0.0.0"
packages = [ { include = "redwood_sdk" } ]
[tool.poetry.dependencies]
python = "^3.8"
``` Layout is standard: `redwood_sdk/__init__.py`, `redwood_sdk/asyncio/__init__.py`, `redwood_sdk/typing/__init__.py`. `pip wheel .` contains the subpackages; `poetry install` editable sometimes only installs the root package. Behavior varies across machines.

josh: Two quick checks: 1) Confirm you're not using implicit namespace packages (PEP 420)  that can confuse installers. 2) Which Poetry version (`poetry --version`)? Older poetry-core had editable regressions.

maria: Not a namespace package (each dir has __init__.py). On broken machines poetry version is 1.5.1; on working machines it's 1.6.0.

sam: That already points to a poetry/core editable regression. But let's add robust packaging metadata so discovery doesn't depend on backend heuristics. Practical fixes: switch to the table form and explicit includes. Example:```toml
[tool.poetry.packages]
include = "redwood_sdk"
```and under `[tool.poetry]` add an `include` globs list: `include = ["redwood_sdk/**", "py.typed"]`. Also ensure `py.typed` exists in package root.

katie: Short-term contributor workaround: use `pip install -e .` (setuptools editable) or `poetry build && pip install dist/*.whl`. We should document preferred dev workflows in onboarding.

maria: I tried `pip install -e .` and it works locally (all subpackages import). `poetry install` editable is flaky. I'll open a tiny PR updating pyproject to use the explicit packages table and include `py.typed`.

ci-bot: CI job 9021 reported unrelated macOS ARM wheel-tag validation error: "ERROR: Invalid wheel tag for platform" (https://ci.example/9021) 

josh: Good plan. Also add a CI smoke test: in a clean matrix job run `poetry install` and then `python -c 'import redwood_sdk.asyncio'` to catch regressions. Add the `pkgutil.walk_packages` diagnostic snippet to the debugging checklist: `python -c "import redwood_sdk, pkgutil; print(list(pkgutil.walk_packages(redwood_sdk.__path__)))"`.

katie: I'll add a short doc in CONTRIBUTING.md explaining editable modes and recommending `pip install -e .` for local dev. I'll also add the CI smoke test once the pyproject PR merges.

maria: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-py/pull/1457 - adds `[tool.poetry.packages]` include, `py.typed` in `include`, and a short contributing note about editable pitfalls. Please review.

sam: Reviewing now. If any contributor still sees missing subpackages after merge, collect: OS, poetry version, pip version, and a minimal repro. We can create a tiny sample repo to reproduce.

josh: One last note: some of the macOS ARM wheel tag errors we've seen in CI are due to runner image/tooling differences (wheel tags produced on musl vs glibc builders). Track that separately.

maria: Thanks everyone. I'll follow up if any outliers remain.

katie: Thanks  will add the docs and CI test after the PR lands. :thumbsup:
